questiontext.text: 1) Which directional cycle correctly organizes the Twelve Primary Channels?

generalfeedback.text: The Primary Channel cycle is chest to hand for Hand Yin, hand to head for Hand Yang, head to foot for Foot Yang and foot to chest for Foot Yin. Why are the other options incorrect? Hand to foot, foot to head, head to chest, chest to hand — This sequence does not match the four Primary directional groups. Chest to head, head to hand, hand to foot, foot to chest — This arrangement reverses and mixes the established group directions. Foot to hand, hand to chest, chest to head, head to foot — This sequence does not preserve the Hand and Foot Yin–Yang cycle.

answer.text: Chest to hand, hand to head, head to foot, foot to chest

feedback.text: The Primary Channel cycle is chest to hand for Hand Yin, hand to head for Hand Yang, head to foot for Foot Yang and foot to chest for Foot Yin.

answer.text: Hand to foot, foot to head, head to chest, chest to hand

answer.text: Chest to head, head to hand, hand to foot, foot to chest

answer.text: Foot to hand, hand to chest, chest to head, head to foot

questiontext.text: 2) Which sequence identifies Divergent Channel organization?

generalfeedback.text: Divergent Channels are recognized by separation, deep entry, paired convergence and rejoining a Yang Primary pathway. Why are the other options incorrect? Begin at a Luo point, cross once, end at the skin — A named Luo-point origin belongs to Luo-Connecting organization. Begin at a digit, bind at joints, remain superficial — Distal origin and joint binding describe Sinew organization. Circle the waist, rise from the heel, end at the eye — This combines features of selected Extraordinary Vessels.

answer.text: Separate, enter deeply, converge with the pair, rejoin

answer.text: Begin at a digit, bind at joints, remain superficial

answer.text: Circle the waist, rise from the heel, end at the eye

questiontext.text: 3) What is the correct relationship between a Luo point and its Luo-Connecting Channel?

generalfeedback.text: A Luo point is the named origin; the Luo-Connecting Channel is the route that departs from it toward its connection and destination. Why are the other options incorrect? They are two names for the same point. — A point and the pathway arising from it are related but not interchangeable. The channel must begin at a Jing-Well point. — Luo routes are not defined by a Jing-Well origin. Every Luo route is a Divergent Channel. — Luo and Divergent pathways have different organization.

answer.text: The point is the origin and the channel is the pathway leaving it.

questiontext.text: 4) Which feature most strongly identifies a Sinew Channel?

generalfeedback.text: Sinew Channels begin distally and spread superficially through muscles, tendons and binding regions without entering the zangfu. Why are the other options incorrect? A deep paired-organ route that rejoins a Yang channel — Deep paired-organ convergence identifies a Divergent route. A branch originating at a Luo point — A Luo-point origin identifies a Luo-Connecting route. A regular point-bearing internal and external course — A regular point-bearing route identifies a Primary Channel.

answer.text: A broad superficial musculotendinous route with joint bindings and no zangfu entry

answer.text: A regular point-bearing internal and external course

feedback.text: A regular point-bearing route identifies a Primary Channel.

questiontext.text: 5) Which geometry identifies the Girdling Vessel?

generalfeedback.text: Dai Mai is distinguished by its transverse course encircling the waist like a belt. Why are the other options incorrect? A posterior point-bearing line from eye to little toe — The posterior eye-to-toe route describes Bladder Primary. A short branch from the lateral lower leg — A short lateral-leg branch may describe Gall Bladder Luo. A medial arm route from chest to little finger — A medial chest-to-little-finger route describes Heart Primary.

answer.text: A transverse belt-like course around the waist

questiontext.text: 6) At the heel, which action correctly identifies the Kidney Luo-Connecting Channel?

generalfeedback.text: The Kidney Luo-Connecting Channel is regionally distinguished by encircling the heel. Why are the other options incorrect? It forms the upper eye net. — The upper eye net belongs to Bladder Sinew. It enters the ear at SI-19. — Ear entry at SI-19 belongs to Small Intestine Primary. It disperses midway between the breasts. — Chest dispersal near REN-17 belongs to Sanjiao Primary.

answer.text: It encircles the heel.

questiontext.text: 7) Which statement correctly distinguishes the Sinew Channels around the eye?

generalfeedback.text: Bladder Sinew forms the upper muscular net and Stomach Sinew forms the lower muscular net. Why are the other options incorrect? Stomach forms both nets. — The nets are divided between two Sinew pathways. Gall Bladder Luo forms the upper net. — Gall Bladder Luo does not form the upper muscular net. Heart Divergent forms the lower net. — Heart Divergent has eye relationships but does not form the named lower net.

answer.text: Bladder forms the upper net and Stomach forms the lower net.

Liver Primary Channel — Liver Primary is included in the diaphragm group.

questiontext.text: 10) Which final response demonstrates mastery of the twelve-objective course?

generalfeedback.text: Mastery requires system classification, regional action, two independent landmarks and explicit rejection of the closest alternative. Why are the other options incorrect? It chooses an organ name from one familiar area. — One region and an organ name cannot distinguish several related systems. It relies on line color and option order. — Color and option position are not anatomical evidence. It turns a regional overlap directly into a diagnosis and treatment. — Regional correspondence alone does not establish diagnosis or treatment.

answer.text: It names the pathway and system, explains the regional action, cites two landmarks and rejects a plausible alternative.
